summary: Find the minimum eating speed k so that all piles are finished within h hours.
mainInsight: The time needed is monotone decreasing in the speed, so binary search the smallest speed whose total hours (sum of ceil(pile / speed)) is <= h; the answer lies in [1, max(piles)].

approaches.name: Binary search on the speed
approaches.summary: Feasible speeds form a suffix; find the smallest.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Use integer ceil (p + speed - 1) // speed instead of float division.

promptVariants: Which pattern solves 'minimum speed so that the task finishes in h hours'?
What is the search space of Koko Eating Bananas?
options: Binary search on the answer (speed in [1, max(piles)])
Sliding window over the pile sizes in their given order
Greedy sorting of the piles then a single scan over them
Heap simulation of every single hour, one hour at a time
cards.answer: Binary search on the answer (speed in [1, max(piles)])
cards.explanation: Feasibility is monotone in the speed: if k works, any larger k works too.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Greedy sorting of the piles then a singl: Order of piles does not matter for the time calculation.

promptVariants: Why is binary search valid on the speed and what are its bounds?
How do you choose low and high?
cards.answer: Total hours is non-increasing in the speed, so 'can finish within h' is false for small speeds and true for large ones. low = 1 (slowest) and high = max(piles) (eating one whole pile per hour is the fastest useful speed; faster does not reduce the ceil-sum).
cards.explanation: A tighter low bound is ceil(sum(piles) / h).

promptVariants: Time complexity (n piles, max pile M): ___
Each of log M iterations scans all piles, giving ___.
cards.explanation: log2(M) feasibility checks of O(n) each.

promptVariants: Why is `ceil(p / speed)` summed, and what is a safer integer form?
cards.answer: Koko finishes a pile in ceil(p / speed) hours because she cannot move to the next pile within the same hour. Float division can be imprecise for large values; use (p + speed - 1) // speed. When time <= h the speed is feasible, so record it and try slower speeds (high = speed - 1).
cards.explanation: Record the answer on feasible speeds.

promptVariants: What is the answer when h equals the number of piles?
How fast must Koko eat if she gets one hour per pile?
cards.explanation: She needs one hour per pile, so the speed must finish the largest pile in one hour.

incorrectOptionExplanations.1: Only if all piles have size 1.
